hero.title: The right loyalty program <accent>for how you actually sell.</accent>
hero.subtitle: Stampeo runs two program types from one wallet card: stamps for repeat visits, points for what customers spend. Here's how each works, and how to choose.

engines.heading: Two ways to reward, one card
engines.subheading: Same wallet card, same setup. The only choice is what you count.

stamps.name: Stamps
stamps.how: Every visit adds one stamp. Fill the card, earn the reward. One tap at the counter, no price to enter.
stamps.bestFor: Best for fixed-price, repeat purchases: coffees, pastries, blow-dries, car washes.

points.name: Points
points.how: Staff enter the amount spent and the customer earns points for it. They spend those points on a menu of rewards you set, up to twelve.
points.bestFor: Best for baskets that vary: restaurants, retail, grocery, specialty shops.

comparison.title: Stamps and points, side by side
comparison.subtitle: Neither is better. They simply fit different businesses.

stamps.title: Go with stamps
stamps.body: Your visits look steady and similar in price, so a punch card is the clearest, most motivating choice.

points.title: Go with points
points.body: Your baskets vary, so rewarding what customers actually spend feels fairer and keeps bigger spenders coming back.

either.title: Either could work
either.body: You're right in the middle. Stamps are the simplest way to start; points are just as quick to set up if you'd rather reward spending.

options.title: The settings that make a program work
options.subtitle: Stamps or points is just the start. You'll meet these dials during setup; here are the four that matter, with our advice for each.

items.name: Start cards pre-stamped
items.description: Hand out cards with the first stamp or two already filled, on the house.
items.tip: A head start works. Customers finish a card they've already begun far more often than one at zero.

items.name: Let rewards stack
items.description: A full card banks its reward and a fresh cycle starts right away. You choose how many rewards a customer can hold.
items.tip: Allow at least two, so nobody stalls because a reward is already waiting.

items.name: Set the rhythm
items.description: You pick the number of stamps, or the point price of each reward, with up to twelve rewards on points.
items.tip: Make the first reward easy to reach. A quick win turns a first visit into a habit.

items.name: Change your mind later
items.description: Switch between stamps and points whenever you want. Your customers keep the same card and their progress.
items.tip: Start simple. Most businesses launch the obvious choice and adjust once real numbers come in.

faq.title: Stamps and points, answered
faq.subtitle: The questions we hear most before choosing a program.

items.question: What's the difference between stamps and points?
items.answer: Stamps count visits: one tap adds a stamp, and a full card earns a reward. Points count spending: staff enter the amount, the customer earns points, and they spend those points on rewards you set. Stamps suit fixed-price repeat visits; points suit baskets that vary.

items.question: Which one should I choose?
items.answer: If your prices are similar and people come back often, stamps are the clearest. If baskets vary or tickets run higher, points reward what customers actually spend. Not sure? Try the picker above.

items.question: Is points more expensive than stamps?
items.answer: No. Both programs are on every plan, Starter included. The card, the wallet updates, and the reward menu cost the same either way.

items.question: How do customers earn points?
items.answer: Your staff enter the amount spent when they scan, and the customer earns points for it, for example one point per euro. You set the rewards and their point price, up to twelve.

items.question: Do my customers need an app?
items.answer: No. The card lives in Apple Wallet or Google Wallet, already on their phone. They scan your QR code once and it's added, stamps or points alike.
